top_story: Israel’s policy trajectory in the occupied Palestinian territories hardened over the past week, moving from the covert approval of a record number of West Bank settlements on 12 May to the expansion of a military-court death penalty regime on 17 May that applies to Palestinians but not Israelis. That escalation unfolded alongside the 14 May Jerusalem Day march, where far-right Jewish nationalists pushed openly violent anti-Arab rhetoric through the Old City, reinforcing a climate in which dispossession, unequal law, and public incitement increasingly operate as parts of the same system. Beyond the West Bank and Jerusalem, Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon on 16–17 May, launched within hours of a ceasefire extension, killed civilians including paramedics and signaled a readiness to override de-escalation arrangements. The combined pattern points to a broader Israeli posture that is not simply managing multiple fronts, but normalizing exceptional force and discriminatory control in ways likely to deepen regional instability and civilian insecurity.
